candidate_relations.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus with renal involvement
candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record establishes SLE with renal involvement as the overarching diagnosis, but the question asks for the most likely diagnosis explaining the non-anion gap metabolic acidosis with hyperkalemia and suppressed aldosterone — which is Type 4 RTA (hypoaldosteronism-mediated). C001 names the parent disease and a component (renal involvement) but does not specify the tubular acidosis subtype that is the reference answer. It is compatible but lacks the required specificity.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: SLE with renal involvement is the underlying etiology/parent condition; the reference diagnosis is the specific acid-base/tubular disorder (Type 4 RTA) arising in this context

case_quality_flags: Reference diagnosis (Type 4 RTA) is a specific complication/manifestation of SLE-related renal tubular dysfunction; the question context makes SLE the background disease and Type 4 RTA the targeted final diagnostic object.
